newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's citrus output to drop by 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's citrus output to drop by 18 pct.

text.p: Morocco's citrus fruit output is expected to drop by about 18 percent to about 1.15 million tonnes in the 1996/97 season compared with the previous season, a farm group spokesman said on Friday.

"The preliminary forecast shows the citrus production for 1996/97 season will be around 1.147 million tonnes," Abdelmoughit Sebbata, a spokesman for the Casablanca-based Societe Agricole de Service au Maroc (SASMA), said.
SASMA said the rich farming area of Souss in southern Morocco would be one of the regions to suffer from the slump.
"This year's forecast drop could be the result of what we call an alternate phenomenon, in general a highly-productive year is followed by a slump," Sebbata said.
The country's citrus export is estimated this season at 525,000 tonnes, down 16 percent on the 1995/96 season, he said.
The harvest season runs from September to June.
